suites.description:

whole queue every five seconds and reconcileHostQueue works out the

suites.description:

disagreeing, so half the app says one name and half says the other.

suites.description:
A 796 song queue drawn whole was 320ms to 2.5s of blocked main thread on
every genuine queue change, and the perf log says that happened 125 times in

gaps.detail: Every rule in src/lib/jukebox.ts is covered, but nothing exercises /api/jukebox/*. The guest seat cookie, the owner access token check and the service-role writes are all unproven by the suite.

buildAlbumFromSongs, the three-pass YouTube search and albumIdentityScore live in a Supabase edge function, not in this repo's build. The workspace copy goes stale, so a test against it would prove something about a file nobody deploys.

spi* is only reachable with a sealed session cookie and a live Spotify account. Nothing covers the /items versus /tracks trap, the notOwned versus reconnect split, or the 429 retry that stops a throttled pass being reported as songs not found.

gaps.gap: Row level security and the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs
gaps.detail: can_edit_track_videos, can_manage_artist, landing_stats visibility filtering and the jukebox_* service-role-only grants are enforced in Postgres. A policy written without a grant verifies nothing, and only a live database can say so.
The three shot lists are checked against each other, but nothing drives Playwright. A shot that silently goes blank because a page global was renamed still only turns up in the morning's images.

gaps.gap: Anything that needs a real YouTube player
gaps.detail: Queue order, shuffle weighting and the Play next override are covered as pure logic. The IFrame API, background play, CarPlay handoff and crossfade timing are not, and cannot be without a browser.
Render functions are asserted by reading their source rather than by mounting them. That catches a deleted guard or a renamed global; it does not catch markup that renders wrong.
set_my_settings carries a new public name onto every credit already written across nine tables. Nothing here proves it reaches all nine.

gaps.gap: Brand art is checked for existence, not for being the right picture
gaps.detail: The suite asserts every path a head points at is on disk. It cannot tell whether the file is the official mark, and on 2026-09-10 it happily passed a header logo built from a crude hand-coded SVG sitting next to the real artwork. A wrong but present PNG is invisible to this suite and obvious to a person.

gaps.gap: The per-surface HTML routes, end to end
gaps.detail: applySurfaceHead is covered against public/index.html, and discoverability.test.mjs pins robots / sitemap / llms.txt shape per surface. Nothing still runs the Next HTML routes themselves: that /community, /share, /share/<slug> and /<slug> return 302 on a playlist-led brand is checked by hand and by curl rather than by the suite.

The hero suite asserts the migration TEXT: that it excludes Spotify, counts only the primary video, scopes to public playlists and de-duplicates the three picks. Nothing executes it against Postgres, so a query that says the right thing and returns the wrong rows would pass. The RPC was verified by hand as anon when it shipped.

lphLoad is stubbed everywhere it is tested. The failure wording, the skeleton-to-cards transition and the single-fetch guard are covered as pure logic; a real 4xx from PostgREST, or a slow one, is not.
